subject: Hosted API pricing: token velocity & peak concurrency qualification
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rojas <elena@lumenexa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing: token velocity & peak concurrency qualification

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and two asks so we can get a scoped hosted quote over to procurement.

Call highlights:
- Use case: conversational customer support + smart summaries for ticket history.
- Target go-live (pilot): mid-August, expand into production by Q4 if pilot metrics hold.
- Key constraints: predictable monthly spend, response P99 latency targets under 600ms, and ability to handle peak bursts from campaign events.

Two items we need you to confirm (these drive both unit economics and whether we recommend reserved capacity vs. purely autoscaled hosted):
1) Expected monthly token volume (best-effort range, e.g., 50M–200M tokens) — this should include both input and output tokens.
2) Peak sustained TPS (tokens per second or requests per second + average tokens per request). If you can give both average and 95th/99th percentile peaks that helps.

Attached I dropped a simple pricing scenario workbook (Redwood-Hosted-Pricing-Scenario.xlsx) with three volume bands and a sample token profile file (Lumenexa-Token-Profile.csv) that you can edit. For budget context, you mentioned a target of roughly $/1M tokens in the ballpark — if you can share that target number that lets us aim proposals at your unit economics (e.g., $700–$1,200 / 1M tokens).

Suggested next steps:
- You confirm the two items above and your preferred $/1M token target.
- We’ll run a quick model and propose 2 options: a committed-banded price (better unit economics, 1–12mo term) and a fully-hosted consumption plan with burst credits.
- If numbers look good, Marissa (cc'd) will loop in Solutions Eng for a short technical session to size concurrency, KV cache expectations, and SLA details.

Would appreciate the numbers today/tomorrow so we can get a quote to procurement by Thursday.

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear recap and the workbook.

Numbers from our side (ballpark, but validated versus analytics):
- Expected monthly tokens: 120,000,000 — 220,000,000 tokens (includes both input and output).
- Average tokens per request: ~650 tokens.
- Average requests per second: ~18 rps (avg), with traffic spikes up to 70 rps during campaign peaks (we measured a 95th percentile of ~55 rps over the last campaign).
  - Converting to tokens/sec at peak: ~70 rps * 650 tokens = 45,500 tokens/sec (approx).
- Budget target: we are aiming for approximately $850 / 1M tokens effective. Procurement is looped for quotes and NDA.

We also need SOC 2 and basic data retention wording for the hosted plan — procurement will flag that on the formal quote.

Elena

Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing: token velocity & peak concurrency qualification

Elena — perfect, this is exactly what we needed. A few clarifications and an initial economics callout so procurement has something to react to quickly: 

Clarifications:
- When you say 70 rps peak, we assume that peak is short bursts (minutes) and 55 rps is your sustained 95th percentile across campaign windows — please flag if we should treat 70 rps as sustained.
- We’ll model both input+output tokens at 650 tokens/request. If you have a separate breakdown we can update.

Initial economics (hosted consumption example):
- Using your $850 / 1M tokens target => $0.00085 per token.
- If we model 150M tokens/month (midpoint of your range) at that rate => ~$127,500/mo.
- For higher volume (220M tokens) => ~$187,000/mo.

Sizing guidance (recommended):
- If your 95th sustained is ~55 rps (35,750 tokens/sec at 650 tokens/request), hosted autoscale with burst credits will likely meet your needs with predictable unit cost.
- For repeated campaign peaks (70 rps sustained for many hours) we typically recommend a small reserved slab for burst capacity to protect against pre-warm latency and reduce per-token unit cost during peaks. We can show a blended banded quote that reduces effective $/1M tokens with a modest reserved commit.

Compliance & SLA: Marissa will attach SOC 2 Type II and our standard hosted data retention language in the formal quote.

Next steps we’ll take today:
- Run two model scenarios in the attached workbook: (A) consumption-only at $850/1M, (B) 6-mo commit with a reserved slab sized for 70 rps peak.
- Draft a short commercial offer (price sheet + procurement checklist) and route it to procurement.
- Schedule a 45-minute technical sizing session — Marissa, can you propose times Wednesday afternoon?

Thanks — we’ll aim to have a formal quote and the two scenario pages back to procurement by EOD Wednesday.

Karthik
